exposure: Maternal antenatal depressive symptoms (measured by EPDS) in the first trimester
Maternal antenatal depressive symptoms (measured by EPDS) in the second trimester
Maternal antenatal depressive symptoms (measured by EPDS) in the third trimester
cohort: The study recruited 2053 pregnant participants from the Sino-Canadian Healthy Life Trajectories Initiative trial in China.
finding: Maternal depressive symptoms in the first or second trimester were associated with a greater risk of macrosomia, while symptoms in the third trimester were linked to higher risks of preterm birth, small for gestational age, and increased infant subscapular skinfold thickness.
